title: In the Morning I Will Pray
description: In the Morning I Will Pray in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Henry Furness wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 364, “Morning Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the morn-ing I will pray For God's bless-ing on the day; What this day shall be my lot, Light or dark-ness, know I not.

lines: In the morning I will pray
For God's blessing on the day;
What this day shall be my lot,
Light or darkness, know I not.
Should it be with clouds o'ercast,
Shine within me, Lord, O, shine!
Show me, if I tempted be,
How to find all strength in Thee,
Keep my feet from secret snares,
Keep mine eyes, O God, from tears!
And my soul from death defend!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Henry Furness died in 1896.
credits: Words by William Henry Furness (1802–1896), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
